utterance: R2 lifecycle: the orchestrator claimed R2 deletes nothing by itself and the photos mirror never ages out; the owner's Cloudflare screenshot shows a bucket-wide lifecycle rule delete-after-30-days that deletes every object 30 days after upload, so the whole photos/current mirror and every dump would vanish 30 days after the last backup if the server stops

disposition.note: Owner approved closing on 2026-10-01 ("PD-48; PD-31; closing COR-1 — i approve these, do it."). Fixed: the owner deleted the delete-after-30-days lifecycle rule; the bucket keeps only Default Multipart Abort Rule and the db-30-days lock.

rootCause: The owner added the bucket-wide lifecycle rule delete-after-30-days following the orchestrator's own earlier R2 setup guidance; the later backup design (rclone sync mirror plus script-side retention of db/ dumps and photos/archive/<date>/) assumes no bucket lifecycle rule, and nobody re-checked the bucket settings against it. Owner, 2026-10-01: "i added this rule using your guidance ... i can remove this rule".
followUp: Owner removes the rule; then the backup status check also reads the bucket lifecycle configuration and alerts on any rule that deletes outside photos/archive/.
fixed: 2026-10-01: the owner deleted the delete-after-30-days lifecycle rule; the bucket keeps only Default Multipart Abort Rule and the lock db-30-days on db/ (owner screenshot). Disposition left for the owner.
